scenarios.title: Tell me about the hike
scenarios.setup: You are back from a hike. Explain why you left later, what you saw, and why the walk was still worth it.
scenarios.starter: ¿Qué tal la caminata? ¿Por qué no salieron más temprano?
twists: The parking lot is full. What do you do?
Tell the same story as a plan for next Sunday.
scenarios.provenance: Pedagogical adaptation of the linked original transcript; new prompts and twists are invented, not verbatim tutor quotes.

scenarios.title: Explain your design work
scenarios.setup: A designer is interviewing you. Explain your work clearly and politely, then retell it to a friend in a relaxed register.
scenarios.starter: Cuénteme algo sobre usted. ¿A qué se dedica?
twists: The interviewer does not understand 3D design. Explain it more simply.
Now ask your colleague for a file.
scenarios.provenance: Pedagogical adaptation of the linked original transcript; new prompts and twists are invented, not verbatim tutor quotes.

scenarios.title: Past jobs and what suited you
scenarios.setup: Discuss an internship, the atmosphere at work, and what you want from your next role.
scenarios.starter: ¿Cómo fue tu primer trabajo? ¿Qué te gustaba y qué no?
twists: Would you choose a higher salary or a better team?
Explain the same job to a formal interviewer.
scenarios.provenance: Pedagogical adaptation of the linked original transcript; new prompts and twists are invented, not verbatim tutor quotes.

scenarios.title: Dinner, payment and tips
scenarios.setup: Your tutor is visiting and asks how you usually eat and pay. Explain your own habits; do not turn class claims into legal facts.
scenarios.starter: Cuando salís a comer, ¿cómo decidís cuánto dejar de propina?
learning_gaps: comida para llevar vs comer fuera
twists: Today you order takeout instead. What changes?
You can only pay in cash. Ask about that.
scenarios.provenance: Pedagogical adaptation of the linked original transcript; new prompts and twists are invented, not verbatim tutor quotes.

scenarios.title: Waiting to move
scenarios.setup: Explain why your move is taking longer than expected and how you are preparing while you wait.
scenarios.starter: ¿Ya está todo listo para la mudanza? ¿Qué falta?
twists: Approval arrives tomorrow. What is your first step?
A friend asks you to explain the delay politely.
scenarios.provenance: Pedagogical adaptation of the linked original transcript; new prompts and twists are invented, not verbatim tutor quotes.

scenarios.title: Plan a trip on a budget
scenarios.setup: Plan a hypothetical trip with your tutor. Choose one destination, a budget, dates and things to do. All prices and access rules are fictional practice details.
scenarios.starter: ¿Adónde te gustaría viajar y con qué presupuesto contás?
learning_gaps: va a costar, not va a acuestar
entrar gratis, not para el gratis
twists: The ticket price goes up. Adjust your plan.
One museum is free on a fictional student day. Ask a follow-up question.
scenarios.provenance: Pedagogical adaptation of the linked original transcript; new prompts and twists are invented, not verbatim tutor quotes.

scenarios.title: Start the lesson naturally
scenarios.setup: Your tutor asks how you are after a busy week. Respond warmly, mention something you did, and ask a follow-up question.
scenarios.starter: ¿Cómo estuvo tu semana? ¿Pudiste descansar un poco?
twists: A friend cancels your plans. Suggest another day.
Retell one good thing from your week.
scenarios.provenance: Pedagogical adaptation of the linked original transcript; new prompts and twists are invented, not verbatim tutor quotes.

scenarios.title: Tell me what they said
scenarios.setup: A colleague asks you to retell a conversation. Use direct quotes and reporting dates from the selected familiar reported-speech cards; change speaker, time and perspective only when the context calls for it.
scenarios.starter: ¿Qué te contó tu compañero? Vamos a reconstruir una de esas conversaciones.
learning_gaps: question words vs si in reported questions
deictic changes: me/nos, llevar/traer, tomorrow/the following day
twists: The person you are talking to changes. Retell the same message from their reference point.
After one successful retelling, change the request to a yes/no question.
scenarios.provenance: Pedagogical adaptation of reported-speech practice in the linked original transcript, supplemented by existing reported-speech cards; prompts and twists are invented, not verbatim tutor quotes.

scenarios.title: Catch up after snowboarding and yoga
scenarios.setup: Your tutor asks why snowboarding still feels difficult even though you have tried it several times. Explain the slope, gear, and what you can do in yoga.
scenarios.starter: ¿Fuiste a la montaña este año? ¿Ya te sale girar sin caerte?
learning_gaps: cada vez que + indicative for repetition
me sale / no me sale; caerse
hace dos años que / a ver si me da tiempo
la vertical vs hacer el pino
twists: Now a friend offers to lend you the equipment: does that change your plan?
You have two hours to teach the tutor one yoga skill.
scenarios.provenance: Pedagogical reconstruction based on redacted Oct 28 transcript; new turns and twists are invented and not exact tutor dialogue.

scenarios.title: Swing class and Halloween plans
scenarios.setup: Catch up with your tutor about a small swing class, social dancing, and a costume party where a friend is performing.
scenarios.starter: ¿Vas a seguir con las clases de swing o preferís ir a bailes sociales?
twists: You meet another dancer who does not know swing. Explain the basic follower role.
Your friend needs help choosing a last-minute costume.
scenarios.provenance: Pedagogical reconstruction based on redacted Oct 28 transcript; new turns and twists are invented and not exact tutor dialogue.

scenarios.title: Finish a mysterious photo story
scenarios.setup: Your tutor gives you the opening of a strange story about a camera. You finish it in the past tense and make a hypothetical revision as the author.
scenarios.starter: Clara vio una figura detrás de ella en la foto. ¿Qué pasó después?
learning_gaps: de golpe, no tener nada que ver con
twists: Make the figure unexpectedly kind rather than threatening.
Retell the ending from the daughter's point of view.
scenarios.provenance: Pedagogical reconstruction from the tutor's picture-story exercise; the details and twists are invented, not verbatim.
